sentences.text:

Court No
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 17403 of 2023

Applicant :- Pankaj
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Brij Lal Shukla
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Syed Ali Imam
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1. Heard Sri Brij Lal Shukla, learned counsel for the applicant; Sri Sanjay Kumar Pal, Advocate
holding brief of Sri S.A. Imam, learned counsel for informant and Sri S. B. Singh, learned Aga for
the State-respondent.

2.  The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
128 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B, 323 IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Jarcha, District Gautam Buddh Nagar, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and his family members and according to the FIR, marriage of the applicant was performed with the daughter of the informant on 6.12.2020 and after marriage applicant and his family members tortured her for Rs. Five lacs and a car and due to non fulfilment of demand of dowry they have committed her murder on 27.7.2022.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is husband of the deceased and on the basis of false allegation of demand of dowry and torture, he has been made accused in the present Pankaj vs State Of U.P. on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68749345/
1 matter.
5.

He further submitted that actually deceased, the wife of the applicant wanted to live in urban area but applicant did not want to leave his family as he wanted to live alongwith his parents and only due to this reason very often dispute arose between husband and wife and one day in anger deceased committed suicide by hanging herself.
6.
He further submitted that even post mortem report of the deceased shows that she died due to hanging.

7. He further submitted that from the perusal of the inquest report which has been annexed alongwith the instant bail application, it reflects that applicant after breaking the door has taken the deceased to the hospital where doctor declared her dead.
8. He further submitted that applicant is having no criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 16.8.2022 i.e. for last almost one and a half year.

9. Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within seven years of her marriage in her matrimonial home under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of demand of dowry and therefore, considering the provisions of Section 304-B IPC and 113 B Indian Evidence Act, applicant should not be released on bail.
10. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
11. However, applicant is the husband of the deceased and his wife died within two years of her marriage in her matrimonial home under abnormal circumstances but

from the post mortem report,
it reflects that deceased died due to hanging and therefore, defence taken by the applicant cannot be brushed aside, at this stage.
12. Further, from the inquest report, it appears that after receiving information that wife of the applicant committed suicide, police arrived at spot and conducted inquest.

13. It further reflects from the inquest report that the constable Manoj Kumar received information that after the incident, applicant after breaking the door of the room of the deceased taken her to the hospital where she was declared dead in the hospital, therefore, inquest report indicates the good conduct of the applicant.
14.
Further, applicant is having no criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 1.8.2022 i.e. for last almost one and a half year.

15. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.

Pankaj vs State Of U.P. on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68749345/
2 16.
Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

17. Let the applicant-Pankaj, be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
18. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

19. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.

Order Date :- 15.12.2023 Ankita  Pankaj vs State Of U.P. on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68749345/
